items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: We were all in music together, we were all in scouting together, and because of that involvement, Pat and John and I are all Eagle Scouts

ctx.x: Your motivation when you were nine or ten was jumpstarted by your father and your brothers. Did your father try to instill some of that reality in you or was it sort of like just a way for the family to be together?

I think it was more of that, Monk, because we as a family did everything together. We were all in music together, we were all in scouting together, and because of that involvement, Pat and John and I are all Eagle Scouts, because my parents were involved in everything that we do, right? So I believe it was more about the family community, the family commitment, and also at that age someone might say I want to be the president or a fireman or whatever, you know, and of course you’re allowed to say that. But as it…

items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I think I was seven and Joe was five, or four. I’m sorry. Joe was four or five. Somewhere along in that line. It’s hard to remember because we were always playing.

ctx.x: And how old were you during the years that this band was active?

I think I started when I was six or seven. If Pat was eight then I was six. And Joe would have been, oh no, I think I was seven and Joe was five, or four. I’m sorry. Joe was four or five. Somewhere along in that line. It’s hard to remember because we were always playing. The family band came much — but my mother at first was not part of the band as you probably know from Pat. But I think when I was about eight we were gigging steadily as a family band.
Did your father write parts for your trumpet playing that — with the fact that you’re seven or eight?
